results.title: Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study - ADS
results.content: ## ADS. ## Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. #### Abstract. Companies adopt agile methodologies and DevOps to facilitate efficient development and deployment of software-intensive products. This, in turn, introduces challenges in relation to security standard compliance traditionally following a more linear workflow. This is especially a challenge for the engineering of products and services associated with critical infrastructures. To support companies in their transition towards DevOps, this paper presents an adaptation of DevOps according to security regulations and standards. We report on our longitudinal study at Siemens AG, consisting of several individual sub-studies in the inception, validation, and initial adoption of our framework based on RefA as well as the implications for practice. RefA is a prescriptive model of a security compliant DevOps lifecycle based on the IEC 62443-4-1 standard. The overall framework is aimed at professionals, not only security experts, being able to use it on implementing DevOps processes while remaining compliant with security norms. We demonstrate how RefA facilitates the transfer of security compliance knowledge to product development teams. This knowledge transfer supports the agility aim of ensuring that cross-functional teams have all the skills needed to deliver the compliant products. : 10.48550/arXiv.2512.14453. : Journal of Systems and Software, Volume 234, 2026, 112718, ISSN 0164-1212.

results.title: [Literature Review] Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study
results.content: This page provides the most accurate and concise summary worldwide for the paper titled Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. [# [Literature Review] Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study](/file? This paper presents a longitudinal study on aligning security compliance with DevOps methodologies, particularly for products and services associated with critical infrastructures. The paper introduces a comprehensive framework designed to facilitate Continuous Security Compliance (CSC) by enabling product development teams to visualize, implement, and assess security practices within their DevOps processes. * **RefA-ArteV (Artefacts View):** Utilizes UML notation to depict the inputs and outputs (artefacts) of DevOps flows, explicitly highlighting those serving as evidence for security compliance. 2. **RefA-AP (RefA-based Assessment Protocol):** A utility guiding the execution of security compliance assessments for DevOps-based processes. It targets the implementation and effectiveness of continuous security practices, allowing assessors to map questions to specific RefA practice areas and identify required artefacts as compliance evidence. It includes four two-hour evaluation sessions covering pairs of DevOps phases, during which assessors use RefA-AQ to determine compliance status, analyze security practices, and request artefact-based evidence. * **RefA-MR (RefA-based Maturity Report):** An instance of the radar chart, depicting the maturity status of security practices per DevOps phase or across the entire lifecycle. This phase established the need to adapt secure development processes for DevOps and enable engineering teams to continuously assess and improve security, specifically targeting the IEC 62443-4-1 standard. **Solution Construction (Studies 3-7):** Iteratively built the framework based on design goals focused on demonstrating security practices in DevOps, enabling IEC 62443-4-1 compliance, and leveraging DevOps for risk-based decision-making. * **R2: Continuous assessment of security compliance is methodologically feasible (and technically possible with automation).** RefA-AP and RefA-MR facilitate frequent, short assessments (within two-week sprints) by DevOps teams with minimal external support. * **R3: Continuous implementation of security compliance is feasible, especially with CI/CD automation.** A "minimally viable product" for security compliance in DevOps was identified, encompassing practices across all DevOps phases. * **R4: Gaps exist between IEC 62443-4-1 and secure DevOps, particularly in covering operational phases (Ops) and continuous integration/delivery (CI/CD) aspects like infrastructure code and SBOMs.** RefA aims to bridge these gaps by incorporating additional best practices.

results.content: # Aligning Security Compliance and DevOps: A Longitudinal Study. **Abstract:** Companies adopt agile methodologies and DevOps to facilitate efficient development and deployment of software-intensive products. This, in turn, introduces challenges in relation to security standard compliance traditionally following a more linear workflow. To support companies in their transition towards DevOps, this paper presents an adaptation of DevOps according to security regulations and standards. We report on our longitudinal study at Siemens AG, consisting of several individual sub-studies in the inception, validation, and initial adoption of our framework based on RefA as well as the implications for practice. RefA is a prescriptive model of a security compliant DevOps lifecycle based on the IEC 62443-4-1 standard. The overall framework is aimed at professionals, not only security experts, being able to use it on implementing DevOps processes while remaining compliant with security norms. We demonstrate how RefA facilitates the transfer of security compliance knowledge to product development teams. This knowledge transfer supports the agility aim of ensuring that cross-functional teams have all the skills needed to deliver the compliant products.
